method: Re-extracted the separately retrieved adopted rules, compared the regular appendix against the dated English catalogue, checked the original thesis and research lab descriptions, then reviewed the frozen record and course evidence.
findings: The 60 EC first year gives access to post-propaedeutic work with positive study advice. The 48 EC Curating the Past major contains seven courses. The two common courses are Philosophy of Art & Culture and The Power of Persuasion II. The third year has 42 EC of electives, a separate 6 EC research lab and a 12 EC thesis. The lab proposal is approved before primary research. The diagnostic test and tutoring add no credits.

The closest option centres objects, art history, museums and cultural politics. Its strongest major-course overlaps are interpretation of objects, revision of art histories, museums and cultural authority, and the circulation of printed and other media. Mapping, archival practice, theatre and the independent thesis retain separate rows. The environmental and digital options correspond to other evidenced interests.

The three schedules fit the active workbook. The environmental option combines cultural inquiry and environmental governance rather than relying on geology. The digital option combines machine learning with media, ethics and culture. The title, notes, sources and schedule-backed course descriptions support the public explanations.
